newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mubarak calls for end to Zaire fighting.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak calls for end to Zaire fighting.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak called on Sunday for an immediate end to fighting in Zaire, warning it had serious implications for Africa's economic and political stability.

Addressing a three-day meeting of the Third World's Group of 15 (G-15) which started in Harare, Mubarak said Egypt welcomed efforts by the international community to stop the violence in the central African country and its surrounding Great Lakes region.
"I must warn that this serious situation in Zaire has serious implications, not only for the Great Lakes region but also for the economic and political stability of Africa," he said.
"We would like to call for the immediate stoppage of the war and for the parties to respect the principles of humanitarianism," he added.

The vast central African country erupted into civil war two weeks ago pitting the Zairean army and allied Rwandan Hutu fighters fighting against Tutsi rebels in the eastern provinces of North and South Kivu facing neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi.
